cleanupOnUninstall.description:
Run a post-delete cleanup Job on `helm uninstall` that removes the leftovers
the worker creates at runtime but Helm does not manage: the Kueue / Node Feature
Discovery / CSI Helm releases, their CRDs, the finalizers pinning Kueue and
Instance objects, and the aggregated APIServices / webhooks. Disabled by default
because those CRDs may be shared with other workloads; enable only when this
release exclusively owns them (e.g. CI / e2e).

apiVersion: config.kueue.x-k8s.io/v1beta2
kind: Configuration
featureGates:
  AssignQueueLabelsForPods: false
  TASBalancedPlacement: true
  # Enables resources.quotaCheckStrategy below (alpha in Kueue 0.18). The bundled
  # controller image is always 0.18, so the gate is always available.
  QuotaCheckStrategy: true
health:
  healthProbeBindAddress: :8081
metrics:
  bindAddress: :8443
# enableClusterQueueResources: true
webhook:
  port: 9443
leaderElection:
  leaderElect: true
  resourceName: c1f6bfd2.kueue.x-k8s.io
controller:
  groupKindConcurrency:
    Job.batch: 5
    Pod: 5
    Workload.kueue.x-k8s.io: 5
    LocalQueue.kueue.x-k8s.io: 1
    ClusterQueue.kueue.x-k8s.io: 1
    ResourceFlavor.kueue.x-k8s.io: 1
clientConnection:
  qps: 50
  burst: 100
#pprofBindAddress: :8083
#waitForPodsReady:
#  timeout: 5m
#  recoveryTimeout: 3m
#  blockAdmission: false
#  requeuingStrategy:
#    timestamp: Eviction
#    backoffLimitCount: null # null indicates infinite requeuing
#    backoffBaseSeconds: 60
#    backoffMaxSeconds: 3600
#manageJobsWithoutQueueName: true
managedJobsNamespaceSelector:
  matchExpressions:
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values: [ kube-system, gpustack-system ]
integrations:
  frameworks:
  - "batch/job"
  - "kubeflow.org/mpijob"
  - "ray.io/rayjob"
  - "ray.io/raycluster"
  - "jobset.x-k8s.io/jobset"
  - "trainer.kubeflow.org/trainjob"
  - "kubeflow.org/paddlejob"
  - "kubeflow.org/pytorchjob"
  - "kubeflow.org/tfjob"
  - "kubeflow.org/xgboostjob"
  - "kubeflow.org/jaxjob"
  - "workload.codeflare.dev/appwrapper"
  - "pod"
  - "deployment"
  - "statefulset"
  - "leaderworkerset.x-k8s.io/leaderworkerset"
#  externalFrameworks:
#  - "Foo.v1.example.com"
#fairSharing:
#  preemptionStrategies: [LessThanOrEqualToFinalShare, LessThanInitialShare]
#admissionFairSharing:
#  usageHalfLifeTime: "168h" # 7 days
#  usageSamplingInterval: "5m"
#  resourceWeights: # optional, defaults to 1 for all resources if not specified
#    cpu: 0    # if you want to completely ignore cpu usage
#    memory: 0 # ignore completely memory usage
#    example.com/gpu: 100 # and you care only about GPUs usage
resources:
  # Kueue is not the authoritative ledger in this operator — the Devices CR
  # is. A ClusterQueue advertises exactly one coarse admission dimension (cpu
  # for general pools, the manufacturer credits for accelerated pools), while a
  # Workload still carries the Pod resources the queue does not cover: memory
  # and ephemeral-storage on every pool, cpu on accelerated pools, and the
  # node-level .sliced.* counters the scheduler/kubelet read. Check only the
  # covered dimension and ignore the rest, instead of refusing to assign a
  # flavor for an uncovered resource (which would mark the Workload inadmissible).
  quotaCheckStrategy: IgnoreUndeclared
  # Credits are scored on the integer base B = D = 1600000 (one whole card = B
  # credits): exclusive→B, shared→B/10, sliced.units→B/D=1 (× multiplyBy
  # .sliced), partitioned.units→B/D=1 (no multiplyBy: a partition request is
  # confined to one card, so its units already carry the whole charge). Every
  # per-mode value stays an integer, so Kueue's ResourceValue int64 quantization
  # (q.Value(), which ceils non-CPU resources) never rounds a fractional credit
  # up to 1.
  #
  # Multiply each manufacturer resource into a single credits resource, so that
  # the queue can be configured with a single credit budget. The multiplyBy
  # factor is the number of credits per unit of the input resource, so that
  # the output credits resource is always an integer. The ".sliced" multiplyBy
  # leaks through unconsumed and the node-level .sliced.* counters pass straight
  # through; quotaCheckStrategy above lets Kueue ignore them.
  #
  # Physical partitions (MIG) count disjoint cards from the logical/sliced
  # family, so those keys are not multiplied by any counting resource: each unit
  # already denotes a fraction of exactly one card.
  # gpustack:chartvalues:kueue-transformations:begin
  transformations:
  - input: amd.com/gpu
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/amd: "1600000"
  - input: amd.com/gpu.shared
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/amd: "160000"
  - input: amd.com/gpu.sliced.units
    strategy: Replace
    multiplyBy: amd.com/gpu.sliced
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/amd: "1"
  - input: huawei.com/npu
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/ascend: "1600000"
  - input: huawei.com/npu.shared
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/ascend: "160000"
  - input: huawei.com/npu.sliced.units
    strategy: Replace
    multiplyBy: huawei.com/npu.sliced
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/ascend: "1"
  - input: cambricon.com/mlu
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/cambricon: "1600000"
  - input: cambricon.com/mlu.shared
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/cambricon: "160000"
  - input: cambricon.com/mlu.sliced.units
    strategy: Replace
    multiplyBy: cambricon.com/mlu.sliced
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/cambricon: "1"
  - input: hygon.com/dcu
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/hygon: "1600000"
  - input: hygon.com/dcu.shared
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/hygon: "160000"
  - input: hygon.com/dcu.sliced.units
    strategy: Replace
    multiplyBy: hygon.com/dcu.sliced
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/hygon: "1"
  - input: iluvatar.com/gpu
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/iluvatar: "1600000"
  - input: iluvatar.com/gpu.shared
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/iluvatar: "160000"
  - input: iluvatar.com/gpu.sliced.units
    strategy: Replace
    multiplyBy: iluvatar.com/gpu.sliced
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/iluvatar: "1"
  - input: metax-tech.com/gpu
    strategy: Replace
    outputs:
      credits.gpustack.ai/metax: "1600000"
  - input: metax-tech.com/gpu.shared
    strategy: Replace

  - input: metax-tech.com/gpu.sliced.units

controllerManagerConfigYaml.description:
Kueue's controller_manager_config.yaml, delivered through the manager-config
ConfigMap. The "resources.transformations" list is generated from `pkg/nodefeature`
by `make generate chart` between its markers; everything else is maintained here.
The managed-jobs namespace selector names "gpustack-system" literally because Helm
merges subchart values instead of rendering them, so the release namespace cannot
reach this string.
controllerManagerConfigYaml.title: controllerManagerConfigYaml

manufacturers.description:
Accelerator manufacturers to manage, mapped to their PCI vendor ID. This is the
single source for the worker `--manufacturer` list, the per-manufacturer device-manager
DaemonSets, the GPUSTACK_<MANUFACTURER>_PCI_VENDOR_ID environment variable propagated
to both the worker and the device-managers, and the vendor IDs the `gpustack-cpu-info`
NodeFeatureRule detects. The manufacturer list is derived from these keys (sorted for
stable rendering); each device-manager DaemonSet only schedules on nodes labelled by NFD
with the matching PCI vendor, so adding an entry here is all it takes for a new vendor's
devices to be labelled, detected and given a device-manager. The defaults are every
manufacturer `pkg/nodefeature` knows, which a Go test asserts and the generated schema
requires; a cluster that carries only some of them runs the other device-managers empty,
since each one only schedules where its vendor label exists.
manufacturers.title: manufacturers

Tolerations for the NFD gc. Defaults tolerate every taint, so stale NodeFeature and

repository.description: NFD image repository; the master, the worker and the gc all run it.
repository.title: repository

annotations.description: Annotations added to the NFD master pods.
annotations.title: annotations

restrictions.description:
What the NFD master is allowed to write. Every value here restates an NFD default,
stated because the whole chain depends on it: labels, taints, annotations and extended
resources all stay enabled, an existing label may be overwritten, and the labels a
NodeFeature asks for are honoured — that last one is how a device-manager's detections
reach its node.

`nodeFeatureNamespaceSelector` is deliberately absent. Pinned to one namespace it makes
the master ignore every NodeFeature created anywhere else, which is exactly what taking
over a cluster's existing NFD must not do: a vendor GPU operator keeps its NodeFeatures
in its own namespace, and they are the features being adopted. Unset means every
namespace, so — together with the two permissive keys above — a NodeFeature anywhere can
influence node labels; `denyNodeFeatureLabels` is the lever that tightens it.
restrictions.title: restrictions

deploymentAnnotations.description: Annotations added to the NFD master Deployment.
deploymentAnnotations.title: deploymentAnnotations

enable.description:
Create a PodDisruptionBudget for the NFD master. Enable it together with `replicaCount`
above; on a single replica it would only block node drains. NFD spells this key `enable`,
not `enabled`.
enable.title: enable

minAvailable.description:
Minimum number of NFD master pods that must stay available, as a count or a percentage.
Keep it below `replicaCount`, or no node can ever be drained.
minAvailable.title: minAvailable

replicaCount.description:
Number of NFD master replicas. The master is what turns a device-manager's detections into
node labels, so while it is down no node is ever (re)classified and the scheduling chain
stalls for new or changed nodes. Above one, NFD's own chart adds `-enable-leader-election`
for you; the standbys watch without writing. NFD's templates render no topology spread
constraints, so spreading these replicas across nodes means setting `master.affinity` — which
replaces NFD's own preference for control-plane nodes rather than adding to it.
replicaCount.title: replicaCount

annotations.description: Annotations added to the NFD master ServiceAccount.
annotations.title: annotations

tolerations.description:
Tolerations for the NFD master. Defaults tolerate every taint, so labelling keeps
working wherever the control plane runs.
tolerations.title: tolerations

annotations.description: Annotations added to the NFD worker pods.
annotations.title: annotations

`gpustack-cpu-info` NodeFeatureRule evaluate.

Only the labels this chart consumes are published, so NFD does not cover the nodes
in features nothing reads.

this same list, so it matches exactly the devices NFD was told to label.
deviceClassWhitelist.title: deviceClassWhitelist

worker.description:
High availability. Every control-plane component this chart deploys elects a leader, so extra
replicas stand by instead of sharing the work: they buy failover, not throughput. A highly
available install raises the replica count of each one and enables the disruption budget that
goes with it — `worker`, `kueue.controllerManager`, `node-feature-discovery.master`, and the
`controller` of both CSI drivers. Spreading those replicas across nodes is per-component and
each key below says what its component supports; the cluster needs as many schedulable nodes as
the largest replica count for a hard spread to be satisfiable. Everything else here is a
DaemonSet, one pod per node already. docs/operation/high-availability.md walks through it.

affinity.description:
Affinity for the worker, replacing the default `preferred` pod anti-affinity that keeps
replicas off one node without ever making one unschedulable.
affinity.title: affinity

certmanager.description: Configure cert-manager integration for the worker webhook serving certificate.

enabled.description:
Whether to issue the worker webhook serving certificate with cert-manager.
Accepts a string (or the equivalent boolean): "auto" creates the cert-manager
resources only when the cert-manager CRDs are detected in the cluster; "true"
always creates them (cert-manager must be installed); "false" never creates
them and the worker generates and manages its own certificate.
enabled.title: enabled

kind.description: Issuer kind ("Issuer" or "ClusterIssuer"); only used when `issuer.name` is set.
kind.title: kind

name.description: Existing issuer name to use; when empty a self-signed Issuer is created.
name.title: name

certmanager.title: certmanager

dataDir.description: Host path mounted at /var/lib/gpustack for persistent operator data.
dataDir.title: dataDir

disableApplications.description:
Applications the worker must not install at runtime, or `*` for all of them. This chart
deploys every one of them itself, so the default takes the worker out of that business
entirely; name individual applications to hand some back to it. The value is templated
rather than appended through `extraArgs` because the flag accumulates across occurrences,
so a second one could only ever disable more. Accepted names: `*`, `kueue`,
`node-feature-discovery`, `csi-driver-nfs`, `csi-driver-s3`, `device-manager`.
disableApplications.title: disableApplications

enabled.description: Deploy the worker (control plane). Disable to deploy only the device-managers.
enabled.title: enabled

env.description: Extra environment variables for the worker, as a name/value map.
env.title: env

extraArgs.description: Extra command-line arguments appended to the worker container args.
extraArgs.title: extraArgs

image.description:
Per-worker image overrides (`repository`/`tag`/`pullPolicy`); unset keys fall
back to the chart-level `image`.
image.title: image

nodeSelector.description: Node selector for the worker; falls back to `global.nodeSelector` when empty.
nodeSelector.title: nodeSelector

enabled.description:
Create a PodDisruptionBudget for the worker. Leave it off on a single-replica install,
where it would only block node drains.
enabled.title: enabled

minAvailable.description:
Minimum number of worker pods that must stay available, as a count or a percentage.
Keep it below `replicas`, or no node can ever be drained.
minAvailable.title: minAvailable

replicas.description:
Number of operator (control plane) replicas. Leader election is always on, so extra
replicas stand by; the reconcilers only ever run in one of them.
replicas.title: replicas

resources.description: Resource requests and limits for the worker container.
resources.title: resources

securePort.description: Secure serving port of the worker container.
securePort.title: securePort

tolerations.description:
Tolerations for the worker. Defaults let the control plane run on
control-plane/master nodes.
tolerations.title: tolerations

topologySpreadConstraints.description:
Topology spread constraints for the worker. This is where node spread belongs: the
default anti-affinity is only `preferred`, on purpose, so three replicas still schedule on a
two-node cluster. An entry that omits `labelSelector` gets the worker's own.
topologySpreadConstraints.title: topologySpreadConstraints

worker.title: worker
